questions.cardText:
[Religious Studies] Towards which city do Muslims face during their prayers?
A. Medina
B. Jerusalem
C. Mecca
Answer: C. Muslims face the city of Mecca during their prayers, specifically the Kaaba, a cube-shaped building that is considered the most sacred site in Islam; it is believed to have been built by the Prophet Abraham and his son Ismail.
questions.de: In Richtung welcher Stadt, in der die Kaaba steht, wenden sich Muslime beim Gebet?
questions.en: Towards which city, home of the Kaaba, do Muslims face during their prayers?

timeline.labelEn: The qibla (direction of prayer) is changed from Jerusalem to the Kaaba in Mecca, in the second Hijri year
timeline.labelDe: Die Gebetsrichtung (Qibla) wird im zweiten Jahr der Hidschra von Jerusalem auf die Kaaba in Mekka umgestellt

questions.notes: Before the change of qibla in the second Hijri year, Muhammad and his followers in Medina prayed towards Jerusalem.

questions.cardText:
[Finance] What does a higher Sharpe Ratio indicate about an investment?
A. Lower expected return
B. Higher risk-adjusted return
C. Higher volatility
Answer: B. Developed by Nobel laureate William F. Sharpe, this ratio helps investors understand how much return they get for the level of risk they are taking, with a higher Sharpe Ratio indicating better risk-adjusted return.
questions.de: Was misst die vom Nobelpreisträger William F. Sharpe entwickelte Sharpe-Ratio bei einer Geldanlage?
questions.en: What does the Sharpe ratio, developed by Nobel laureate William F. Sharpe, measure for an investment?

timeline.labelEn: William F. Sharpe introduces the reward-to-variability ratio, later called the Sharpe ratio
timeline.labelDe: William F. Sharpe führt die Reward-to-Variability-Ratio ein, die später Sharpe-Ratio genannt wird

questions.notes: Also accepted: excess return per unit of risk (volatility).
